A1.justification: Both complete, readable 20-page PDFs describe AliTok, with matching authors, core architecture and ImageNet experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revision and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original ImageNet generation, reconstruction, component ablations, training curves and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original generation and reconstruction results, revised ablations and training curves, plus new decoder attention analyses in Figures 8 and 11.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 substantially revises prefix-token training: 17 prefixes become 16, and the MSE-only auxiliary loss becomes MSE plus perceptual loss, using prefix reconstructions concatenated with gradient-detached remaining rows. The auxiliary weighting changes, and second-stage buffer tokens increase from 32 to 64. The underlying causal-decoder and two-stage framework remains.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate on ImageNet-1K for 256×256 class-conditional generation and reconstruction. The attention analyses and replacement visualization examples introduce no distinct dataset, domain or task scenario. OpenImages was only discussed as other work's training data in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes DiT-XL and VAR-d20 while retaining the other generation comparators. Table 4 replaces MaskGIT and VAR with CVQ-VAE and GigaTok-B-L; TiTok-B is retained as TiTok-B-64 with identical settings and score. V1's additional VAR reconstruction comparison in Table 5 is also removed.

E3.justification: The reported evaluation protocols change substantially: v1's 5,000-image PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS evaluation and tokenizer compute/timing evaluation disappear, while v2 adds local 3×3 attention averaging and selected-token analysis. Sampling temperatures change from 0.98/0.99/0.97 to 0.95, guidance scales from 16/6/13 to 11/5/8, and some schedule powers change. Main training budgets, splits and 50,000-image FID evaluation remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds a substantive mechanism analysis comparing baseline and AliTok bidirectional-decoder attention, testing whether causal preference survives unrestricted decoding (Figures 8 and 11). Table 3 retains the component-ablation structure but evaluates the revised prefix/loss design, and Figure 7 replaces the reconstruction example. The 400-versus-800-epoch analysis is retained and updated, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's mean attention maps summarize activations rather than uncertainty in experimental outcomes.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces AliTok-B/L/XL guided gFIDs of 1.50/1.42/1.35 with 1.44/1.38/1.28; XL unguided gFID changes from 1.84 to 1.88. These accompany revised tokenizer and sampling settings. Ablation results, training curves and throughput values also change; final rFID changes from 0.84 to 0.86 and reconstructed-training-set FID from 1.21 to 1.15. Attention findings are added, while v1 Table 5's quality and efficiency results disappear.

T1.justification: Appendix Equation (5) substantively redefines the training objective: v1's alpha × (Nprefix/Nremain) × Laux + Lrec, with alpha=10, becomes Lrec + Laux. The autoregressive factorization and vector-quantization definitions remain unchanged. No theorem or proof is added; the new entropy discussion is explanatory.

C1.justification: The central contributions—aligning token dependencies with autoregression and enabling competitive standard decoder-only generation—remain. The introduction strengthens the specific guided-gFID claim from matching LightningDiT at 1.35 to surpassing it at 1.28 versus 1.35. The contribution list also explicitly bounds the diffusion-model comparison to ImageNet.

C2.justification: V2 adds an unseen-future/high-entropy explanation and interprets attention asymmetry as evidence that contextual information is organized within causal history. It removes v1's dataset-bias and face/hand-generation limitations, together with the explanation of inferior LPIPS performance. The codebook bottleneck interpretation is retained and moved into Appendix A.1.

D1.justification: Positional-index and loss-weight specifications are revised, and the stated GAN implementation source changes from SDVAE to Open-MagViT2. V2 omits the ConvNeXt-S perceptual-network identification and explicit exclusion of Top-k/Top-p sampling. Hardware, model configurations and the code/weights access link remain documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Janus, Janus-Pro, NextStep-1, Wan and discriminative codebook priors, while removing references including DINO, OpenImages, DiT, SDXL and PixelRNN. The central positioning of adapting token sequences to standard autoregression remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, ablation discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The title drops 'AliTok:', references move before the appendices, and the discussion and separate appendices are reorganized into Appendix A subsections. Author-year citations and an LLM-use disclosure are introduced.

P2.justification: V2 adds attention-map Figures 8 and 11, redesigns Figure 2, revises the architecture diagram and training plots, and replaces Figure 7's typewriter example with a harp. V1 Table 5 is removed, other tables are revised or relocated, and typography and running headers change throughout. Most generation galleries and the supplementary reconstruction montage are retained and moved.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and the new attention analyses strengthen support for the central mechanism. However, v2 removes v1 Table 5's broader reconstruction and efficiency evidence, including the LPIPS weakness, and drops specific limitations. Lower headline gFID accompanies changed methods and sampling settings. These gains and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall paper quality.
